lessons.title: Coffee and Espresso Drinks
lessons.body: To make good take-away coffee, start with freshly roasted beans, ground just before brewing. In many African cities, you can buy local robusta or arabica from markets or roasters like Nairobi's Java House or Lagos' CafÃ© Neo. For a strong espresso, use a ratio of 1:2 coffee to water: 18g of ground coffee yields about 36g of espresso in 25-30 seconds. If you don't have an espresso machine, a moka pot or French press works. For take-away, pre-heat cups with hot water, then dry them. Serve espresso in 4oz cups, Americano in 8oz, and lattes in 12oz. Milk: whole milk steams best to 60-65Â°C; oat or soy milk also works but may need more practice. For iced coffee, brew double-strength, cool quickly, and serve over ice in a 16oz cup. Sweeten with sugar syrup, not granulated sugar, so it dissolves in cold drinks. Popular African twists: add a pinch of cinnamon or cardamom, or use condensed milk for a sweeter, creamier taste. Always lid securely and offer a sleeve for hot cups. Keep coffee beans in an airtight container away from sunlight. Clean your equipment daily to avoid bitter oils. With practice, you can serve cafÃ©-quality drinks from a small stall.

lessons.title: Iced Teas and Lemonades
lessons.body: Iced teas and lemonades are cheap to make and sell well in hot African climates. For iced tea, brew black tea (like Kenyan or Rwandan tea) at double strength: use 4 tea bags per litre of hot water, steep 5 minutes, then remove bags. Add sugar while hot (about 100g per litre), then cool. For lemonade, mix fresh lemon juice (about 6 lemons per litre), 150g sugar, and 1 litre water. Stir until sugar dissolves. For a hibiscus (zobo) iced tea, boil dried hibiscus leaves with ginger and pineapple peels, strain, sweeten, and chill. Serve all drinks over plenty of ice in 16oz or 20oz cups. To keep ice from melting too fast, use large cubes or crushed ice packed tightly. Add fresh mint, lemon slices, or fruit chunks for appeal. For take-away, pre-mix in large jugs and pour into cups with lids. Offer straws. Cost per cup: iced tea about 20-30 cents, lemonade 30-40 cents; sell for 1-1.50 USD. Make in small batches to avoid spoilage; discard after 24 hours. Use clean water and wash lemons well. During peak heat, these drinks can outsell hot coffee. Keep a cooler with ice and pre-chilled drinks for quick service.

lessons.title: Smoothies and Fresh Juices
lessons.body: Smoothies and fresh juices are high-margin items. Invest in a good blender (at least 1000W) and a juicer if possible. For a basic smoothie, use 1 cup fruit (mango, banana, pineapple, or berries), 1/2 cup yogurt or milk, 1/2 cup ice, and 1 tablespoon honey or sugar. Blend until smooth. For a green smoothie, add a handful of spinach or kaleâit doesn't change taste much but adds nutrition. For fresh juice, use a juicer or blend and strain. Popular African juices: mango, pineapple, watermelon, passion fruit, and ginger. For ginger juice, blend fresh ginger with water and strain; mix with pineapple juice for a spicy kick. Always use ripe fruit for sweetness. To save money, buy fruit in bulk at local markets when in season. For take-away, pour into 16oz cups with lids. Add a wide straw for smoothies. Keep juices cold in a cooler or fridge. Sell within 24 hours; shake before serving. Cost per cup: smoothie about 50-70 cents, juice 40-60 cents; sell for 2-3 USD. Offer combinations like mango-pineapple or watermelon-ginger. Clean blender and juicer immediately after use to prevent staining and bacteria. Use gloves and wash fruit thoroughly.

lessons.title: Hot Chocolate and Specialty Drinks
lessons.body: Hot chocolate is a comfort drink that sells well in cooler mornings and evenings. Use real cocoa powder or dark chocolate, not just sugary mixes. For one 12oz cup: heat 1 cup milk (or water) until steaming, whisk in 2 tablespoons cocoa powder and 2 tablespoons sugar (adjust to taste), and a pinch of salt. For a richer drink, melt 30g dark chocolate into the hot milk. Stir until smooth. For a spicy African twist, add a pinch of chili powder, cinnamon, or nutmeg. For a mocha, add a shot of espresso. For a white hot chocolate, use white chocolate. Specialty drinks can include chai tea (black tea with milk, sugar, and spices like ginger, cardamom, and cinnamon) or a turmeric latte (warm milk with turmeric, ginger, and honey). For take-away, use 12oz or 16oz cups with lids. Pre-mix dry ingredients in batches to speed up service. Keep milk hot but not boiling (about 70Â°C). Offer whipped cream or marshmallows for an extra charge. Cost per cup: about 40-60 cents; sell for 2-3 USD. Clean your whisk and pots regularly. These drinks have a high perceived value, so they can boost your profits.

lessons.title: Packaging and Temperature Control
lessons.body: Packaging makes or breaks a take-away beverage business. For hot drinks, use double-wall paper cups with lidsâthey keep drinks hot and hands safe. For cold drinks, use clear plastic cups with dome or flat lids. Buy in bulk to reduce costs: 1000 cups with lids may cost 50-80 USD. Consider eco-friendly options like bagasse or paper straws if your customers care. Temperature control: for hot drinks, pre-heat cups with hot water, then fill. Use a thermos or insulated carrier to transport. For cold drinks, use a cooler with ice packs. Never mix hot and cold in the same cooler. For smoothies and juices, keep fruit and pre-made drinks in a fridge at 4Â°C or below. If you don't have a fridge, use a cooler with ice and rotate stock. For hot drinks, hold coffee at 80-85Â°C, but never reheat more than once. For cold drinks, serve at 2-4Â°C. Label cups with drink name and date if pre-made. Train staff to lid cups tightly and test for leaks. Offer napkins and stirrers. A clean, organised packaging station speeds up service and reduces waste. Always store cups and lids off the floor and in a dry place.

lessons.title: Upselling and Combo Deals
lessons.body: Upselling increases your average sale without new customers. Train staff to suggest a larger size, an extra shot, or a flavour syrup for just 50 cents more. For example, when someone orders a coffee, ask, 'Would you like a pastry with that for only 1 USD more?' Combo deals bundle a drink with a snack: coffee + mandazi for 2.50 USD, or smoothie + samosa for 3 USD. Create 2-3 combos and display them on a chalkboard or menu. Use suggestive selling: 'Our fresh mango smoothie is very popular todayâwould you like to try it?' Offer loyalty cards: buy 5 drinks, get 1 free. This builds repeat business. For take-away, suggest a cold drink with a hot meal, or a hot drink with a cold snack. Keep add-ons visible near the till: cookies, muffins, or extra shots. Price combos so the customer saves 10-15% compared to buying separately. Track which combos sell best and adjust. During peak hours, have a staff member dedicated to upselling at the pickup point. Remember, upselling should be friendly, not pushy. A simple 'Would you like to make that a large for 50 cents more?' can raise your revenue by 20-30%.

quiz.q: What is the ideal ratio of coffee to water for espresso?
quiz.explanation: Espresso typically uses a 1:2 ratio, e.g., 18g coffee to 36g espresso.

quiz.q: What temperature should milk be steamed to for lattes?
quiz.explanation: Steaming milk to 60-65Â°C brings out sweetness without scalding.

quiz.q: Which sweetener dissolves best in cold drinks?
quiz.explanation: Sugar syrup mixes easily into cold liquids, unlike granules.

quiz.q: How many tea bags per litre for double-strength iced tea?
quiz.explanation: 4 tea bags per litre gives a strong brew that holds up over ice.

quiz.q: What is a common African ingredient for iced tea?
quiz.explanation: Hibiscus (zobo) is widely used in African iced teas.

quiz.q: How much lemon juice per litre for lemonade?
quiz.explanation: About 6 lemons yield the right tartness for 1 litre.

quiz.q: What should you do to prevent ice from melting too fast?
quiz.explanation: Large cubes melt slower, keeping drinks cold longer.

quiz.q: How long can you keep pre-made iced tea?
quiz.explanation: Discard after 24 hours to avoid spoilage.

quiz.q: What is a key tool for making smoothies?
quiz.explanation: A blender combines fruits, ice, and liquids into a smooth texture.

quiz.q: Which fruit is commonly used in African smoothies?
quiz.explanation: Mango is abundant and sweet in many African countries.

quiz.q: What should you add to a green smoothie for nutrition without changing taste?
quiz.explanation: Spinach blends well and is mild in flavour.

quiz.q: How should you store fresh juice for take-away?
quiz.explanation: Keep juices cold in a cooler or fridge to maintain freshness.

quiz.q: What is a popular African juice combination?
quiz.explanation: Watermelon-ginger is refreshing and common in many regions.

quiz.q: How much cocoa powder for a 12oz hot chocolate?
quiz.explanation: 2 tablespoons of cocoa powder give a rich chocolate flavour.

quiz.q: What spice adds an African twist to hot chocolate?
quiz.explanation: A pinch of chili powder adds a spicy kick popular in some regions.

quiz.q: What is chai tea typically made with?
quiz.explanation: Chai is black tea brewed with milk, sugar, and spices like ginger and cardamom.

quiz.q: What temperature should milk be kept at for hot chocolate?
quiz.explanation: 70Â°C is hot enough without boiling, preserving taste.

quiz.q: What is a good upcharge for whipped cream?
quiz.explanation: A 50-cent upcharge is common and profitable.

quiz.q: What type of cup is best for hot take-away drinks?
quiz.explanation: Double-wall cups keep drinks hot and protect hands.

quiz.q: What is the ideal holding temperature for hot coffee?
quiz.explanation: 80-85Â°C keeps coffee hot without burning.

quiz.q: How should you store cups and lids?
options: B) In a dry place off the floor
quiz.explanation: Store in a dry, elevated area to prevent contamination.

quiz.q: What is a good combo deal?
quiz.explanation: Coffee and mandazi is a popular and profitable pairing.

quiz.q: How much should a combo save the customer?
quiz.explanation: A 10-15% saving encourages combo purchases.

quiz.q: What is a loyalty card tactic?
quiz.explanation: Buy 5 get 1 free is a common and effective loyalty offer.

quiz.q: When is the best time to upsell?
quiz.explanation: Upselling at the point of order is most effective.

quiz.q: What is a suggestive selling phrase?
options: B) 'Our mango smoothie is popular today.'
quiz.explanation: Suggestive selling highlights a popular item to encourage purchase.

quiz.q: What should you do if you don't have a fridge for cold drinks?
options: B) Use a cooler with ice
quiz.explanation: A cooler with ice maintains safe cold temperatures.

quiz.q: How often should you clean your coffee equipment?
quiz.explanation: Daily cleaning prevents bitter oils and bacteria.

quiz.q: What is a key benefit of offering combo deals?
quiz.explanation: Combos increase the average transaction value.

quiz.q: What should you do with leftover smoothies at the end of the day?
